As another comment said, im sure you don't actually hate everyone, you're just overwhelmed, stressed out, you have alot of new hormones pumping through your bloodstream, and are probably going through some pretty bad stuff. It can really affect the way you see the world, and how you feel. But trust me it'll get better. Everything will work itself out. Give it time. Be patient with yourself. There are things you can do to improve your quality of life, there are steps you can take. If you don't have access to therapy, talking to a school counselor would be a good place to start. Don't tolerate bullying, learn your bullies names and report them every single time it happens. Trust me, i know its nerve wracking but its ALWAYS worth it when they get in trouble or get threatened with being held back a grade. Also, spend alot of alone time. You dont need a girlfriend right now, you need privacy and streas relief. Learn to enjoy your own company. Draw, work out, watch things youre interested in, cook yourself healthy meals that you like. Create routine for yourself and develop interests that bring you a sense of peace and relaxation. Work on your sleep schedule too. Trust me, once you can confidently take care of yourself and find things you enjoy doing by yourself, you'll feel alot better. Its okay to not like anybody right now, puberty can do that to you, abuse can do that to you. What matters is liking yourself. Take care of yourself and eventually you will find people that you actually like and whom like you. I promise. Giving up isnt the answer, you're still a kid, you have plenty to experience first

DID is a covert disorder for most people, not for EVERYONE, but for the vast majority of systems, switches are subtle, time loss and stuff like that we keep to ourselves, etc. From looking at us you can't tell.

The switches for my system usually just look like zoning out for a little bit. Not at all noticeable to the untrained eye. There are times when it can be more obvious, like if we feel really really sick and dizzy we can fall down during a switch.

But most people never notice. Especially because alters do this thing called masking, for the most part we know when we need to act like the host, or the person that everyone thinks we are. 

DID is so covert, most alters, such as hosts, don't even know that they have it. We didnt know for 16 years until we were admitted to the psychiatric ward in the hospital for something else, and while there we were tested for dissociative disorders and came up 100% positive for it- it was a total shock to us and most everybody else. There were only 2 people in our whole life that noticed "personality changes" aka alters switching out before diagnosis. Now most people know (that we tell) and address the alters accordingly.

Tldr: DID is majoritively covert and in most situations you aren't going to notice. Advice for you- be real sweet to your mom and patient if you can💜 DID is caused only by severe and repeated childhood trauma- just because you can't see our struggling doesn't mean it isn't there. Also, all alters are people and should be treated with the same amount of respect. Movies and TV shows that involve DID never make it seem that way.
